<!-- /ask-widget/ -->
ask-widget provides a floating chat interface, a streaming response adapter and
headless hooks. Use the supplied widget or compose your own interface around
`useChat`, `useSSEStream` and `useSession`.

## Start with a working example

Follow [Getting started](/ask-widget/getting-started) to install the scoped package and
render a demo. Then connect a backend using the [SSE contract](/ask-widget/backend), or
supply a custom response handler from the [API reference](/ask-widget/api).

## Choose your integration

- [Next.js and Vite](/ask-widget/integrations): client boundaries and stylesheet imports.
- [Theming](/ask-widget/theming): light/dark presets and custom colors.
- [Standalone hooks](/ask-widget/hooks): custom UI and browser-local persistence.
- [Troubleshooting](/ask-widget/troubleshooting): missing styles, network failures and history.

## Read with an agent

Use Copy Page for a guide’s Markdown, `/ask-widget/llms.txt` to discover pages,
and `/ask-widget/llms-full.txt` for the full published documentation. Examples
are reference material; verify commands against your installed package version.

## Contribute

Read [Architecture](/ask-widget/architecture), [Development](/ask-widget/development) and
[Maintenance](/ask-widget/maintenance) before changing the package. Release history is
available in [Changelog](/ask-widget/changelog).

---

<!-- /ask-widget/api -->
# API reference

## ChatWidget props

Props are generated from the installed repository source. `streamResponse` takes precedence over `apiUrl` and `apiToken`; no backend props selects demo mode.

ChatWidget props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `apiUrl` | `string \| undefined` | `—` | Base URL of your chat API. When provided (without a custom \`streamResponse\`), the widget will automatically use \`useSSEStream\` to connect to \`\<apiUrl\>/v1/chat\` with an OpenAI-compatible payload. |
| `apiToken` | `string \| undefined` | `—` | Bearer token for API authentication. Browser-visible token. Use only a short-lived token scoped to your backend. Keep private provider credentials on the server; frontend environment variables do not conceal secrets. |
| `position` | `ChatPosition \| undefined` | `bottom-right` | Position of the floating button and chat panel. |
| `theme` | `ChatTheme \| undefined` | `dark` | Color theme preset. |
| `colors` | `ChatColors \| undefined` | `—` | Custom color overrides - merged with theme defaults. |
| `title` | `string \| undefined` | `Ask AI` | Title shown in the chat panel header. |
| `placeholder` | `string \| undefined` | `Ask me anything...` | Placeholder text in the message input. |
| `initialMessage` | `string \| undefined` | `Hello! How can I help you today?` | First message displayed when the panel opens. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean \| undefined` | `false` | Whether the chat panel starts open. |
| `labels` | `ChatLabels \| undefined` | `—` | Custom text labels for technical indicators in the UI. |
| `persistenceKey` | `string \| undefined` | `ask_widget_session` | The localStorage key used to persist chat history. |
| `streamResponse` | `ChatStreamHandler \| undefined` | `—` | Custom response handler - takes full control of streaming. Use this when you need custom fetch logic, auth flows, or a non-SSE backend. When provided, \`apiUrl\` and \`apiToken\` are ignored. |

## `ChatStreamHandler` Type

If you have a non-standard API or require custom fetch logic, you can pass a `streamResponse` handler:

```ts
export type ChatStreamResult =
  string | AsyncIterable<string> | Promise<string | AsyncIterable<string>>;

export interface ChatStreamContext {
  signal: AbortSignal;
}
export type ChatStreamHandler = (
  message: string,
  history: ChatMessage[],
  context?: ChatStreamContext,
) => ChatStreamResult;
```

### Example Usage

```tsx
import { ChatWidget, type ChatStreamHandler } from '@chitrank2050/ask-widget';

const streamResponse: ChatStreamHandler = async (message, history) => {
  const response = await fetch('/api/chat', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify({ message, history }),
  });
  if (!response.ok) throw new Error('Chat request failed');
  return response.text();
};

export function Assistant() {
  return <ChatWidget streamResponse={streamResponse} />;
}
```

This example expects a plain-text response from your own backend. For token streaming, use the [SSE adapter](/ask-widget/backend) or return an async iterable that decodes your backend’s stream.

---

<!-- /ask-widget/architecture -->
This document describes the high-level architecture and design of `@chitrank2050/ask-widget`.

## Component Layer

The main entry point is the `ChatWidget` component. It renders a floating chat action button and a collapsible chat panel containing:

- **Message List**: Renders conversation history as plain text with user/assistant message variants.
- **Input Area**: Captures user text and manages the submission state.

## State & Hooks Layer (Headless API)

The business logic is decoupled from the UI using custom hooks:

- `useChat`: Manages state for the conversation (messages array, loading state, input state).
- `useSSEStream`: Connects to the SSE streaming API and streams tokens sequentially.
- `useSession`: Manages state persistence across page reloads using `localStorage`.

## Style & Presentation Layer

The UI is styled using Vanilla CSS with CSS Cascade Layers (`@layer`) to organize style precedence; CSS layers do not provide selector isolation. Variables are driven by HSL tokens conforming to the neutral zinc palette.

---

<!-- /ask-widget/backend -->
## Keep credentials on the server

The widget does not host a model or authenticate users. Your server owns provider
credentials, user authorization, rate limits and request validation. Browser
`apiToken` values are visible to users; use only short-lived, scoped credentials.

## Built-in adapter

`apiUrl` is concatenated with `/v1/chat`. For a same-origin backend, `apiUrl=""`
does not select the adapter: use `useSSEStream({ apiUrl: '', path: '/api/chat' })`
and pass its `streamResponse` to `ChatWidget`.

```tsx
'use client';
import { ChatWidget, useSSEStream } from '@chitrank2050/ask-widget';
import '@chitrank2050/ask-widget/styles.css';

export function Assistant() {
  const { streamResponse } = useSSEStream({ apiUrl: '', path: '/api/chat' });
  return <ChatWidget streamResponse={streamResponse} />;
}
```

The default body contains `messages` and `stream: true`. The default extractor
reads `choices[0].delta.content` from JSON data lines and stops on `[DONE]`.
The path is an ask-widget convention, not a promise that every provider exposes
`/v1/chat`. Adapt `path`, `buildBody` and `extractChunk` to your backend.

The parser accepts multiline JSON data events, optional spaces after `data:`,
CR/LF line endings and UTF-8 characters split across network chunks. It also accepts
an unterminated final JSON frame at EOF. It does not implement EventSource
reconnection or retry fields.

`useChat` supplies history including the current user message exactly once. The
default request body uses that history without duplicating the prompt. A standalone
adapter call can supply prior history; the adapter appends the prompt unless it is
already the last user message.

## Cancel a response

Closing the panel, pressing Escape or resetting the conversation cancels the active
response. `useChat` also exposes `cancelResponse()`. The built-in adapter aborts
fetch and cancels its reader. Custom handlers receive an optional third argument
with an `AbortSignal`; pass it to your network request:

```tsx
import type { ChatStreamHandler } from '@chitrank2050/ask-widget';

const streamResponse: ChatStreamHandler = async (message, history, context) => {
  const response = await fetch('/api/chat', {
    method: 'POST',
    signal: context?.signal,
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify({ message, history }),
  });
  if (!response.ok) throw new Error('Chat request failed');
  return response.text();
};
```

Existing two-argument handlers continue to work. Their late results are ignored
after cancellation, but stopping custom network or server work requires the handler
to honor the signal.

## Cross-origin requests

A remote backend must allow your website origin, POST requests and any required
headers in its CORS policy. Do not disable browser security to work around CORS.

## Custom protocols

Supply a [ChatStreamHandler](/ask-widget/api#chatstreamhandler-type) when your response
format differs. It can return text, a promise of text or an async iterable of
text chunks. Rendered message content is plain text; Markdown rendering is not
part of the current widget.

## Published releases

Read [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/chitranklabs/ask-widget/releases) for
published versions and release notes. The repository’s

<!-- /ask-widget/development -->
## Install

Use Node.js 24.14 or newer and the repository’s pinned pnpm version.

```bash
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm build:lib
```

## Run the website

```bash
pnpm dev
```

The website runs at `http://localhost:3006`. Rebuild the library after editing
widget source because the website consumes its emitted package exports.

## Run the documentation

```bash
pnpm docs:dev
```

Open `http://localhost:4181/ask-widget/`. Documentation is built by Monoline Docs
independently of Next.js. The `/ask-widget/` base preserves existing GitHub Pages
URLs. API props are extracted from component source before the documentation build.
Restart docs development after changing widget prop declarations to refresh the table.

## Verify

```bash
pnpm test
pnpm typecheck
pnpm build:lib
pnpm docs:build
```

Do not commit `docs/dist`, package `dist` or website `.next` output.
The website and documentation have separate deployment targets; docs output is
never mounted into the Next.js application.

## SEO and deployment

The website is deployed independently to `https://askwidget.chitrankagnihotri.com`.
For Vercel, set the project Root Directory to `website` and enable source files
outside the Root Directory. `website/vercel.json` builds the library before Next.js
and does not build or deploy documentation.

Set `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` to that production origin; canonical URLs, social URLs,
robots and the sitemap use the same value. Vercel previews emit `noindex` and disallow
crawling. The sitemap omits modification dates until real page revision dates are available.

Monoline Docs deploys to `https://chitranklabs.github.io/ask-widget/`. Its `site`,
`base` and `seo` configuration control canonical URLs, social metadata, publisher
identity and the sitemap. Keep this base while existing Pages URLs are in use.
A project site does not own the host-root `/robots.txt`; its sitemap is under the
project base. The website's `llms.txt` links to the Docs Markdown exports.

Run `pnpm --filter ask-widget-website test:seo` against a production build, or set
`TEST_BASE_URL` to an existing local server to check its rendered metadata.

Identity synchronization is explicit: run
`pnpm --filter ask-widget-website sync:identity` to refresh the checked-in fallback,
then review the result. Normal development and production builds do not rewrite
that file from a remote response.

`build:lib` verifies ESM and CommonJS public exports, SSR rendering and both
stylesheet aliases after emitting the bundle. CommonJS output uses `.cjs` because
the package is declared as an ES module.

## Website and documentation theme

The website and documentation share `assets/theme.css`. The palette follows the widget’s neutral zinc surfaces. Change semantic colors there to keep both sites consistent in light and dark mode. Website layout and component styling live in `website/src/app/globals.css`; the Docs site loads the shared stylesheet through `docs/monoline-docs.yml`. The published widget has its own theme and can be customized with its `theme` and `colors` props.

The website declares Tailwind’s reset and UI layers before the widget layers in `globals.css`. Keep that order when changing stylesheet imports; host resets must not override the widget’s composer, buttons or message styles.

The website uses Monoline UI for buttons, labeled inputs, segmented selections, navigation, footer, theme switching and separators. Keep workbench layout local to the website. Its code examples compose Monoline CodeBlock with explicit Prism highlighting and custom asynchronous clipboard feedback; do not enable Prism’s automatic DOM scanning before React hydration.

## Repository cleanup

Run `pnpm obliviate` to select build output, dependencies, caches or lockfiles.
Build and dependency cleanup covers the library, website and docs workspaces.
Lockfile deletion is a separate, explicit choice because it resolves the dependency
graph again on the next install. Do not clean output while its preview is running.
The menu propagates failed commands as a nonzero exit status.

Use `pnpm git` to prepare a release PR through GitHub Actions or inspect recent
release runs. Publishing and recovery follow the maintenance guide.

## Website domain migration

The production website uses `https://askwidget.chitrankagnihotri.com`.
Keep both the new domain and `ask-widget.chitrankagnihotri.com` attached to the same
Vercel project. The host-specific rule in `website/vercel.json` permanently
redirects requests from the old hostname to the matching path on the new hostname.
It does not redirect local development or Vercel preview hostnames.

Set the production `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` to the new origin and redeploy. Verify the new property and sitemap in Google Search Console. Keep the old hostname’s DNS and TLS working for existing links.
The npm package name, repository name and GitHub Pages documentation base remain
`ask-widget`; they are independent of the website hostname.

## Website analytics

The website uses Cloudflare Web Analytics while hosting stays on Vercel.
Set `NEXT_PUBLIC_CLOUDFLARE_ANALYTICS_TOKEN` in the Vercel project’s Production
environment to the public beacon token for `askwidget.chitrankagnihotri.com`, then
redeploy. No token is stored in source. A missing token disables the integration;
an invalid token fails the production build with a configuration error.

The script loads after hydration only in production. Local development and Vercel
previews do not send analytics. The beacon measures traffic and Core Web Vitals;
there is no separate Vercel Analytics, Speed Insights or Umami reporter. Keep
Cloudflare’s automatic script injection off when using this manual integration
to avoid duplicate beacons. The published widget does not include analytics.

---

<!-- /ask-widget/getting-started -->
**ask-widget** is a lightweight React component for adding a streaming AI chat assistant to your developer portfolio. It’s strictly monochrome by default and designed to align with the popular "zinc/neutral" aesthetic.

## Installation

```bash
# with npm
npm install @chitrank2050/ask-widget

# with pnpm
pnpm add @chitrank2050/ask-widget

# with yarn
yarn add @chitrank2050/ask-widget
```

## Registry choice

Use the npm distribution for the styled React widget; it includes the compiled
stylesheet and its `styles.css` and legacy `style.css` aliases. The JSR distribution
publishes TypeScript source and hooks. JSR does not support CSS module entry points,
so the npm stylesheet aliases are not available there. Use npm when following the
styled widget examples below.

## Basic Usage

To use the widget, render it at the root of your application (or any top-level layout).

```tsx
import { ChatWidget } from '@chitrank2050/ask-widget';
import '@chitrank2050/ask-widget/styles.css';

export default function App() {
  return (
    <main>
      <ChatWidget
        apiUrl="https://your-api.example.com"
        position="bottom-right"
        theme="dark"
        title="Ask Anything"
      />
    </main>
  );
}
```

## Prerequisites

To enable real chat streaming, you'll need an API that supports Server-Sent Events (SSE). By default, `ask-widget` expects an OpenAI-compatible endpoint at `/v1/chat` that accepts a `POST` request with a `messages` array in the body.

If you don't have a backend ready yet, the widget will automatically run in **demo mode** (interactive mocked responses).

## Authentication

Keep private provider API keys on your server. The widget sends requests from
the browser, so `apiToken` is visible to the person using the page. Vite
`VITE_*` and Next.js `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` variables are public client configuration,
not secret storage.

Point `apiUrl` at your own backend, or use `streamResponse` for an authenticated
application endpoint. If your backend requires a browser bearer token, use a
short-lived token scoped to that user and endpoint, not a private provider key.

Use `@chitrank2050/ask-widget/styles.css` for the widget stylesheet. The older
`style.css` export remains supported for existing consumers.

---

<!-- /ask-widget/hooks -->
**ask-widget** is more than just a component-it's a collection of headless hooks that you can use to build your own completely custom chat interface.

## `useChat`

Manages chat state, message history, and the streaming lifecycle.

```tsx
import { useChat } from '@chitrank2050/ask-widget';

const {
  messages,
  isStreaming,
  latency,
  activeStreamId,
  inputValue,
  setInputValue,
  sendMessage,
  clearHistory,
  cancelResponse,
} = useChat({
  initialMessage: 'Hi! How can I help?',
  streamResponse: async function* (message) {
    yield message.toUpperCase();
  },
});
```

## `useSSEStream`

Handles the SSE connection, fetch headers, and token parsing from compatible SSE APIs.

```tsx
import { useSSEStream } from '@chitrank2050/ask-widget'

const { streamResponse } = useSSEStream({
  apiUrl: "https://my-api.com",
  path: "/v1/chat",
  // also takes customizable body builders and chunk extractors
})

<MyCustomUI onSend={(msg) => streamResponse(msg, history)} />
```

## `useSession`

A simple hook to handle message persistence to `localStorage`.

```tsx
import { useSession } from '@chitrank2050/ask-widget';

const { messages, setMessages, clearSession } = useSession('my_chat_session');
```

The hooks must run inside a React component or custom hook. `useSession` takes
a persistence key and optional initial messages; it does not accept an options
object. Treat persisted chat history as browser-local data, not secure storage.

`cancelResponse()` stops the current response without clearing completed messages.
`clearHistory()` cancels before resetting. Custom handlers can use their optional
abort context as shown in [Backend and SSE](/ask-widget/backend#cancel-a-response).

Persisted messages are validated before restoration. An unavailable storage API
falls back to in-memory state; changing the session key loads that conversation
without copying the previous conversation into its storage entry.

---

<!-- /ask-widget/integrations -->
## Next.js App Router

Wrap the interactive widget in a client component and import its stylesheet:

```tsx
'use client';
import { ChatWidget } from '@chitrank2050/ask-widget';
import '@chitrank2050/ask-widget/styles.css';

export default function Assistant() {
  return <ChatWidget title="Ask about this project" />;
}
```

Render `Assistant` from your layout. This example runs demo responses. Connect
your own endpoint using the [backend guide](/ask-widget/backend). Keep private provider
keys in server-only environment variables.

## Vite React

```tsx
import { ChatWidget } from '@chitrank2050/ask-widget';
import '@chitrank2050/ask-widget/styles.css';

export default function App() {
  return <ChatWidget />;
}
```

The published package declares React and React DOM 18 or newer as peers.
Vite `VITE_*` variables and Next.js `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` variables enter browser code;
they are suitable for public configuration, not private credentials.

## Multiple widgets

Give independent conversations distinct `persistenceKey` values. Otherwise they
share the same browser-local history key. Configure positions so launchers do not
overlap. The widget does not synchronize conversation state between open tabs.

---

<!-- /ask-widget/maintenance -->
## Prepare a release

Use Conventional Commits; Lefthook and git-hygiene validate commit messages.
Run **Release 1 - Prepare PR** to calculate the next version and open a
`release/v<version>` branch. The PR updates `package.json`, `jsr.json` and the
generated `CHANGELOG.md` together.

## Finalize

Merging a labeled release PR starts **Release 2 - Finalize Tag**. The workflow
verifies matching versions, runs library tests and types, builds the package and
checks its packed contents before creating the tag. A conflicting existing tag
fails explicitly; it is never overwritten.

npm, JSR and the GitHub release run independently against the verified source
commit. npm publishes only the root library, with provenance. JSR publishes its
source package using OIDC. GitHub release notes come from git-cliff for that tag.
Documentation deployment remains a separate main-branch workflow.

## Recover a failed destination

Dispatch **Release 2 - Finalize Tag** with the exact version and a `target`:
`npm`, `jsr`, `github` or `all`. Manual recovery requires an existing tag and selects its immutable source
commit. If tag creation failed, rerun the original merged-PR build/tag job rather
than creating a recovery tag from the current main branch. Published npm versions and existing GitHub releases are retained;
JSR skips versions already published. Registry or authentication errors remain
visible failures.

For a new npm publication, run the workflow from the release tag so the workflow
commit and package source match the provenance statement. Recovery from another
workflow ref can restore GitHub or JSR, or skip an already published npm version,
but cannot publish a new npm version with mismatched provenance.

The separate JSR recovery workflow also requires an existing version tag and
checks both version files. Do not edit a released version or move a published tag;
make a new release for source changes. Publishing still requires npm credentials
or its configured trusted publisher, and the JSR repository/OIDC association.

## Verify locally

```bash
pnpm test
pnpm lint
pnpm typecheck
pnpm build:lib
npm pack --dry-run
```

Use `deno publish --dry-run --allow-dirty` to validate unpublished JSR changes
without publishing them. The dirty-tree flag is for this local dry run; CI
publishes a clean, verified source checkout.

Operational configuration lives in `.github/workflows/`, the bot action in
`.github/actions/setup-bot/`, `lefthook.yml` and `cliff.toml`.

<!-- /ask-widget/theming -->
**ask-widget** comes with a premium, monochrome design based on the "zinc" and "neutral" color palettes popular in the modern developer ecosystem.

## Built-in Themes

You can toggle between `dark` and `light` themes with the `theme` prop:

```tsx
<ChatWidget theme="light" />
```

## Custom Colors

If you need to align the widget's colors with your personal site, you can pass a `colors` object:

```tsx
<ChatWidget
  colors={{
    primary: '#f43f5e' /* Accent color for bubbles and buttons */,
    background: '#09090b' /* Background color of the chat panel */,
    text: '#fafafa' /* Main text color */,
    border: '#27272a' /* Border colors for the widget */,
    userBubble: '#18181b' /* Background of user messages */,
    surface: '#111113' /* Background of input and system chips */,
  }}
/>
```

### Note on Custom Colors

These values are applied as CSS variables to ensure they are consistent across the UI. They will override the theme defaults for both `dark` and `light` presets.

---

<!-- /ask-widget/troubleshooting -->
## The widget is unstyled

Import `@chitrank2050/ask-widget/styles.css` once in your application. Ensure your
build includes CSS assets; importing only headless hooks does not provide your
custom interface with styles.

## Demo responses appear instead of real responses

Without a custom `streamResponse` or a non-empty `apiUrl`, the component selects
the built-in demo. See [Backend and SSE](/ask-widget/backend) for same-origin requests.

## Requests fail or responses stay empty

Inspect your browser’s network panel. Check the final URL, response status,
CORS headers and your backend’s authentication requirements. The default adapter
expects JSON data lines with `choices[0].delta.content`; change `extractChunk`
for a different payload. Never include credentials when sharing diagnostics.

## History is shared or does not survive a reload

Set a distinct `persistenceKey` per conversation. Browser storage may be disabled
or unavailable in private browsing. Saved history is local to the browser and
origin; it is not server synchronization or secure storage.

## A custom response continues after closing the panel

Close, Escape and reset cancel the active chat request and ignore late results.
Pass the handler's optional `context.signal` to fetch to stop its network work too.
See [Cancellation](/ask-widget/backend#cancel-a-response). Existing handlers that ignore the
signal cannot have their remote work forcibly stopped by the widget.
